topInterview.title: INTERVIEW
topInterview.content:
[Lotus Painting]

This work was done by Brittany Deng ‘24 when she was nine years old. She chose to paint a lotus flower because she lovedflowers, and her mom had told her that lotuses symbolize strength and resilience. The flower rises up from the mud anddifficulty, and blooms to be beautiful, and Brittany felt like that represented her family’s story as immigrants to theUS. The painting is dedicated to her mom.

Audrey Zhang ‘25

Audrey ‘25became a young artist at four and has loved visual arts ever since. Not limited by a single media, sheenjoyed painting, drawing, craft making, and even animating. Since Audrey did not own a phone when she was young, she would sketch in her sketchbook whenever she wanted to capture a scene. She enjoyed the power to create something of her own and hold on to it forever.

Audrey’s favorite piece of art from her past self is an animation she created at the age of 10. It featured a frame-by-frame stop motion of a man turning into a bird, inspired by Wallace Stevens’s poetry “Thirteen Ways of Looking at a Blackbird.” This work embodied both her love of visual art and her appreciation of literature.

When asked about how she viewed her past artworks, Audrey responded, “I really enjoy looking back at them, because they remind me of my younger self. I’ve always thought of art to express emotions, and emotions are temporary, but art makes them permanent.” Being able to transform moments into memories was her favorite aspect of creating art when she was young.

Sagata Das ‘25
Sagata ’25 has been creating art for as long as she can remember: “I feel like as soon as I could hold a pencil, I created art– whether it was for a school project or a doodle on my homework.” She focused on traditional art until she was introduced to the world of digital art and started drawing using the trackpad on her laptop on Microsoft Paint. With the book series Warrior Cats being her most significant influence, cats became her main subject of interest.

Sagata used to feel embarrassed when looking back at the art created by her younger self, especially the pieces she used to brag about. Now, she simply laughs it off and focuses more on her improvements. One of her favorite pieces of digital art she created was a drawing of a dragon, as it demonstrated her courage to go out of her comfort zone by creating something more complex than her typical choice of subjects, with the addition of a complete background.

Sagata loved creating art because it introduced her to a new way to express creativity. Although she used to feel pressured by “child prodigies” who created picture-perfect drawings resembling photography, it never let her passion for art die off. She claims that “even if I’m not the best artist, what matters the most is that I enjoy it.”

Timothy Hebard ‘24

Tim ’24 has always liked to draw, as he started his artistic endeavors with coloring books. Soon enough, coloring booksbecame doodles and doodles developed into drawings. There was a time period where Tim stopped drawing, and he sometimeswondered what his art might look like today if he stuck with art. Despite this, he is happy with the pieces he currentlycreates. Tim’s favorite aspect of drawing is how it allows him to convert his imagination into tangible images. Heexpressed how “there is something truly special about moving an image from mind to page.”
